proposal.statement: High ambient temperatures combined with strong solar insolation can cause the resistors in a digital instrument transformer to overheat to temperatures that exceed safe operating limits.
proposal.passage: Thus, if a sealant with thermal conductivity λ1 is used, the temperature of the most warmed up resistor rises from 58 to 115 ºС (an increase of 57 ºС), the peak temperature being attained at 5 pm. Using a sealant with thermal conductivity λ2 resulted in an even sharper increase in temperature -from 73 to 183 ºС (an increase of 110 ºС). It should be noted that a temperature of 183 ºС is inadmissible for transformer operation.
proposal.impact_mechanism: elevated ambient temperature and solar radiation increase the heat load on transformer resistors
proposal.impact_outcome: resistor temperatures rise to levels that are unsafe for transformer operation
